title: 200,000 Antelope Dropped Dead in Just a Few Weeks

scenes.text: It took only a few weeks, right in the middle of calving season.
That wiped out more than 60 percent of the world's saigas.
The killer was a bacterium that normally lives harmlessly in their tonsils.
Researchers think hot, humid weather let it flood into their blood.
Two hundred thousand animals. A few short weeks.

description:
In 2015, 200,000 saiga antelope dropped dead.
The die-off took a few weeks and killed more than 60 percent of the species. A normally harmless bacterium, Pasteurella multocida, is blamed, probably helped along by hot, humid weather.
Could one germ really do this? Tell us below.
first_comment: Did you know saiga antelope exist? Most people have never heard of them. Tell us if you had.
